To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) in patients with Brugad syndrome arrhythmias induced by programmed ventricular stimulation were associated with future ventricle arrhythmia risk; 2) induction with fewer extrastims were associated with higher risk; 3) clinical risk factors were important determinants of ventricular arrhythmias; and 4) lack of induction did not necessarily portend a low ventricular arrythmia risk, particularly in high-risk patients.
